title: Why You Pull Away the Moment Someone Gets Close
description:
The relationship is finally good. They reach for your hand and say they really like you — and something in you goes cold. The flaws appear. You want distance. You're not afraid of commitment. A survival strategy you learned before you had words is running on its own.

This is the avoidant attachment pattern: a blueprint built in childhood that mistakes closeness for danger and distance for truth. It doesn't announce itself as fear. It arrives as a grown-up conclusion — this isn't enough, this is too fast, I do better alone.

Referenced: Bowlby, Attachment and Loss (1969) · Ainsworth et al., Patterns of Attachment (1978) · Hazan & Shaver (1987) · Bartholomew & Horowitz (1991) · Cassidy & Kobach (1988).

Autopilot makes calm, research-grounded explainers about the predictive brain — why you think, feel, and act the way you do. No hype, no quick fixes. Just the mechanism.

This video is for education only and is not psychological advice.
